summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — KER.PA +14%, CRDA.L +8%, UNA.AS +8%, WKL.AS +7%, RHM.DE +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (RMS.PA -12%, IFX.DE -6%, ASM.AS -5%, PHIA.AS -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: KER.PA (+14.31%) — Q2 2026 earnings beat: Gucci's sales decline slowed to -2% (vs -4% est), H1 revenue returned to growth after 12 quarters; sparked broker upgrades (HSBC to Buy, PT €340) and a two-day rally. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — KER.PA is a large-cap French luxury/consumer-discretionary conglomerate (CAC 40), likely excluded if uk-eu universe skews toward UK-listed or non-luxury sectors. Even if covered, the move was a pre-market earnings gap (results released before Paris open 7/28) that a post-open re
top_movers.suggestion: Expand uk-eu universe to include CAC 40/major Euronext Paris large-caps by market cap, and add an earnings-day gap rule that releases names with pre-open results showing post-print gap ≥10% for same-day entry consideration.

top_movers.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded CRDA to 'Overweight' on 7/30, capping a re-rating after H1 results beat (organic sales +4.6%, Beauty Actives +19%) and a Citi PT hike on 7/29.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — CRDA.L is a UK specialty-chemicals large-cap (FTSE 100), a sector/cap bucket not covered by the uk-eu strategies' tradable lists.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 specialty-chemicals names to the uk-eu universe, or add a sell-side-upgrade scanner that pulls in any index constituent hit with a same-day broker upgrade + prior-week earnings beat.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 results beat (5.8% underlying sales growth vs 4.3% est, EPS €1.61 vs €1.59 est) + raised FY26 guidance, reported 2026-07-28; two sell-side price-target hikes (BofA, TD Cowen) extended the rally into 2026-07-30.
top_movers.miss_reason: UNA.AS is a mega-cap, low-beta EU consumer-staples name — outside any active strategy's universe, likely because those universes skew toward smaller/higher-beta liquid names or exclude defensive staples. The move was also a 2-day-old post-earnings drift, not a fresh same-day signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift scanner that flags large-caps with cumulative gap ≥5% over the 2 trading days following results, so late-drift continuation in mega-cap staples isn't missed just because the news broke pre-open two sessions ago.

top_movers.catalyst: No specific same-day news found; move likely reflects continued re-rating after JPMorgan's Jul 9 Overweight upgrade (PT raised to €87 on 'AI moat' thesis) ahead of Aug 5 HY results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — WKL.AS is a large-cap (~€30-35B) Dutch info-services/publisher on Euronext Amsterdam. Likely excluded not by size but because universes are built from fixed sector/index constituent lists that don't cover diversified publishing/professional-info names.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AEX blue-chip / diversified-info-services constituents to the uk-eu universe build, or add a sector-agnostic mega-cap (>€20B) inclusion rule so names like WKL.AS aren't dropped purely for missing a sector tag.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 earnings beat: core profit ~€562M (~2x YoY, +20% vs est), revenue +70% to €3.3B, order backlog surpassed €80B — shares jumped ~9% on the print.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RHM.DE is a German defense/arms manufacturer (DAX, ~€53B cap); likely screened out by a sector/ESG 'controversial weapons' exclusion rather than a cap or liquidity filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Audit the sector-exclusion list: if defense names are blanket-excluded on ESG grounds, add an explicit allowlist override for DAX/FTSE defense primes (RHM.DE, BA.L) so earnings-gate logic can still evaluate them.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 trading update: revenue growth accelerated to +11% (£2.06B), cloud-native +25%, AI/Sage Intacct momentum; FY guidance reiterated
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SGE.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap enterprise software name; uk-eu strategies appear scoped to smaller/mid-cap or non-software sectors, so a scheduled pre-market trading-update gap-up on a name never in the watchlist couldn't be caught regardless of signal quality.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 enterprise-software/SaaS constituents (SGE.L, and peers) to the uk-eu universe, or add an earnings-gate rule admitting any FTSE 100 name with a scheduled trading update showing accelerating YoY revenue growth ≥10% for same-day review.

top_movers.catalyst: H1/Q2 2026 results (Jul 29): revenue grew ~6-7% cc but FX cut ~€360m and operating margin fell ~40bps, disappointing a market pricing in more; shares fell ~10-12%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RMS.PA is a EUR-denominated, ultra-high-priced (>€1,400/share) CAC40 luxury megacap; static uk-eu universe lists likely exclude it on price/sector screens even though it's highly liquid.
top_movers.suggestion: Add CAC40 luxury megacaps (RMS, MC, KER) to the uk-eu universe and wire an earnings-day gap-gate that flags any constituent with a post-results open gap ≥7% for same-day review, regardless of static list membership.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector contagion: STMicroelectronics plunged ~14% on disappointing guidance, dragging European chip peers; IFX also oversold (RSI ~29) into its Aug 5 Q3 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IFX.DE is a DAX-listed EUR semiconductor large-cap; the uk-eu book's universe likely excludes European chip names or names in an earnings quiet period, so a peer-driven sector cascade never entered scoring.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX semiconductor constituents (IFX.DE, plus peers) to the uk-eu universe and add a sector-contagion trigger: flag names moving >=5% same-day when a same-industry peer moves >=10% on an earnings reaction.

top_movers.catalyst: Record Q2 revenue (€1.003B) and raised FY guidance, but new orders/bookings missed estimates and AI-capex financing worries drove a sell-the-news drop into today's close, two sessions post-earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ASM.AS is an AEX-listed Dutch semicap (ALD/Epi) equipment maker not covered by uk-eu strategies, likely excluded via narrow sector/country coverage or an earnings-blackout filter around its Jul 28 report.
top_movers.suggestion: Add major Euronext Amsterdam semicap names (ASM.AS, BESI.AS) to the uk-eu universe, gated by a post-earnings drift rule that flags T+1/T+2 moves ≥5% when headline beats mask an orders/bookings miss.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-earnings drift: Q2 report (Jul 28) beat EPS but showed -1% comparable order intake and China procurement weakness; analysts cut price targets Jul 29-30, extending the selloff.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PHIA.AS is a large-cap Dutch medtech/healthcare name on Euronext Amsterdam, likely excluded if the uk-eu universe is scoped to UK-listed or a narrower EU sector list rather than all major Amsterdam bellwethers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add major Euronext Amsterdam/Paris healthcare large-caps (incl. PHIA.AS) to the uk-eu universe, and add a T+3 post-earnings-drift scanner flagging names with negative order/guidance surprises even after the initial report day.
